q1_issues.issue: The bare-plural generic subject 'nightmoths' is put in the consequent's Agent slot as the bare kind symbol, so the avoidance never reaches any individual nightmoth, whereas the generic-subject doctrine ('Birds fly' plus the one-premise-per-universal rule) would range it as a second premise (Member $m nightmoth) with a two-argument Skolem event; the bare-class-symbol licence covers non-specific objects, not subjects.

q2_gaps: A bare-plural generic subject appearing in the CONSEQUENT of a whenever/every-time rule: the instruction set's whenever example has a definite constant subject ('the dog barks') and never states whether a generic plural there becomes a second universal premise, a per-occurrence group witness, or a bare kind filler
notes: Otherwise clean: inanimate transitive subject correctly Agent, burn's object Patient, avoid's object Theme, 'that lantern' bound to the premise variable, and 'alongside' rendered as the surface-preposition oblique Alongside, which the open-class oblique licence permits.
